root_cause: Single-shot generation with no execution feedback: empty-result queries are returned unchecked (over-strict equality/LIKE filters, wrong column or join direction), and projection width is guessed without guidance
what: Turn solve.py into a draft -> execute -> repair loop: run the first query, and if it errors or returns zero rows, make one repair call that includes the schema, question, the failing SQL and its result, plus generic relaxation advice (LIKE/case-insensitive matching, verify literal values and FK join direction). Add Spider-style projection guidance to the system prompt (bare 'which X' entity questions want all columns of the entity table; explicit attribute lists stay narrow) and raise max_tokens so the reasoning model still emits a final sql block.
decision: s1 delivers the largest measured gain (83.33 -> 93.33) with zero broken tasks, and its mechanism — execute-then-repair on error/empty results plus generic projection guidance — is domain-general rather than task-specific; s2's regex-based column/value sampling adds more brittle complexity for a smaller gain (90.0) and missed two of its three predicted fixes.

root_cause: One-shot generation never checks the draft against real DB values: literal mismatches (sp0536 'Bachelors', sp0610 title) and unverified empty results (sp0894 wrong column names) silently return 0 rows
what: Add a second policy call that is only spent when the first draft fails to execute or returns zero rows; it shows the failing query plus actual sample values of the columns referenced in the draft so the model can correct literals/joins/columns. Also strengthen the system prompt with general rules about matching stored value formats, anti-join semantics for 'no/without' questions, and minimal column selection.

root_cause: Projection width is guessed by a blanket 'whole entity -> SELECT *' rule: attribute words naming real columns are expanded to all columns, and joined-table columns are dropped when gold keeps them
what: Replace the '*' heuristic in system_prompt.md with explicit projection rules (resolve attribute words like details/name/number against actual schema column names before falling back to '*'; for questions spanning several tables with no named attributes keep every joined table's columns), and add a generic column-count consistency check in solve.py that spends the spare policy call on suspicious projections, feeding back the produced columns and the full column lists of the referenced tables.

root_cause: Projection width is decided from surface wording: 'details' collapses to one table's columns while gold wants every joined table, and an attribute word naming a real column gets expanded to '*'
what: Replace the blanket 'whole entity -> SELECT *' bullet in system_prompt.md with an explicit projection procedure: resolve attribute words against actual schema column names first (so 'details for the paragraph ... text' picks Paragraph_Text), and when no attribute resolves, select all columns of every table needed to answer (T1.*, T2.*), not just the primary entity. Only this projection rule changes; nothing else in the prompt or code is touched.
decision: It is the only admissible candidate and delivers a clean +3.34pt gain (96.67 vs 93.33) with zero broken tasks, fixing sp0362 — one of the two projection failures the r0 execution-feedback loop repeatedly missed (P1).
